equity.level_reason: Percentages of high-incidence counties are reported by racial/ethnic composition group and interpreted as potential impact on communities of color, but values are only set side by side with no computed difference or ratio, so the level is capped at 2.

level_alternative.reason: The report is framed around disparities and names systemic social, economic and environmental inequities as causes; rankings ('larger percentage') could be read as a quantified contrast.

ev.q: Counties whose percentage of racial and ethnic minority persons exceeded the 2019 national percentage were considered to have relatively large populations

determinants_of_health.v: long-standing systemic social, economic, and environmental inequities

equity.equity_measurement: Ecologic: groups are counties whose minority-group share exceeds the national percentage; county groups overlap and are not compared with counties without large minority populations; no case-level race data.

notes: Ecologic design is inferred from the county unit of analysis; the report names itself only a population-based analysis. Jenks natural breaks and the >100 per 100,000 threshold are cutpoints (quantization), not procedures.
